feedback: The geometry changes to a narrower wheel_track of 0.13 and smaller sensor_size of 0.008 have both benefits and challenges. The narrower wheel_track improved turning agility as intended, but the race telemetry shows the controller had to reduce base_speed to maintain stability, indicating a trade-off between agility and control. The smaller sensors provided sharper line edge detection, which helped reduce sensor overlap and improved signal clarity, but also required increasing the proportional gain (kp) to respond effectively to the clearer but weaker signals. The damping gain (kd) needed to be increased to counteract steering oscillations that persisted despite the geometry improvements. The sensor x-coordinate adjustments by ±0.005 optimized sensor coverage, but the controller still compensates for some residual oscillations and occasional line loss events, especially on the s-bend track. Overall, the geometry helped by providing more precise sensor data and quicker physical response, but the controller had to adapt gains carefully to balance agility and stability. For next iterations, I request the following specific geometry changes: 1) Increase wheel_track slightly to 0.135 to regain some stability lost at 0.13 while preserving improved agility; 2) Keep sensor_size at 0.008 to maintain sharp edge detection; 3) Adjust sensor x-positions by ±0.007 to further optimize sensor spacing and coverage, potentially reducing residual oscillations and line loss events. These changes aim to find a better balance between agility and stability, enhancing controller performance and reducing off-track failures.
requested_changes: wheel_track: 0.135 to improve stability while retaining agility
sensor_size: keep at 0.008 for sharp edge detection
sensor_positions x-coordinates: adjust by ±0.007 to optimize sensor coverage and reduce oscillations
